answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small bond in a shared haven — a bonded registry where reputation is earned only through verified work over time. Newcomers start with a tiny allowance, and a beacon service publishes every identity's trust history so buyers can check it before paying. Like yarrow spreading slowly by root, trust grows gradually and cannot be faked overnight: spinning up ten throwaway identities means ten bonds and ten slow histories, so farming stops paying.
